summary: Iran appoints Mohsen Rezaei as Supreme Leader's representative to the Supreme National Security Council while imposing six maximalist conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, linking Gulf energy transit to conflicts in Gaza, Lebanon, Yemen, and Iraq. Netanyahu rejects the Trump administration's 15-point Gaza plan, demanding complete Hamas disarmament and ruling out a Palestinian state. Hamas reaffirms commitment to the mediator roadmap, creating a diplomatic impasse as US-coordinated oil flows through the Strait continue at 8 million barrels nightly.

sections.executive_summary: Iran appoints Mohsen Rezaei as Supreme Leader's representative to the Supreme National Security Council while imposing six maximalist conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, linking Gulf energy transit to conflicts in Gaza, Lebanon, Yemen, and Iraq. Netanyahu rejects the Trump administration's 15-point Gaza plan, demanding complete Hamas disarmament and ruling out a Palestinian state. Hamas reaffirms commitment to the mediator roadmap, creating a diplomatic impasse as US-coordinated oil flows through the Strait continue at 8 million barrels nightly.

points: Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei appointed Mohsen Rezaei, former IRGC commander (1981-1997) and current military adviser, as his representative to the Supreme National Security Council, replacing Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr who was shifted to political adviser role. (Source: @VahidOnline/77795, @Faytuks_Network/6190)

Iran's Supreme National Security Council declared six conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz: cessation of US attacks on Iran and allies in Lebanon, Palestine, Yemen, Iraq; lifting naval blockade; withdrawal of US forces from around Iran; payment of war damages; lifting sanctions; release of frozen assets. (Source: @VahidOnline/77788)

IRGC spokesperson stated Strait reopening depends solely on US acceptance of Iran's conditions, denying linkage to Oman-mediated talks; Zolghadr emphasized the Strait will not open until all six demands are met. (Source: @VahidOnline/77788, @mamlekate/104107)

Foreign Minister Araghchi affirmed Iran is not negotiating with the US and will not negotiate or open the Strait until the US ceases breaching the previous Memorandum of Understanding; Iran-Oman talks only cover future arrangements after US compliance. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/6178)
Unverified claim that Iranian regime attacked a ship with a drone overnight; no location or confirmation provided. (Source: @rodast_omiddana/79040)
Reports indicate a drone shot down in southern Iranian airspace belonged to Saudi Arabia. (Source: @naya_foriraq/87425)

Prime Minister Netanyahu explicitly rejected the Trump administration's 15-point Gaza peace plan, vowing no Israeli withdrawal until Hamas is fully disarmed, defining disarmament as elimination of all heavy, medium, and light weaponry. (Source: @VahidOnline/77790)

Netanyahu stated Israeli security is non-negotiable, acknowledged talks with US officials but deemed some American ideas unacceptable, and ruled out a Palestinian state in Gaza or West Bank as long as he remains premier. (Source: @VahidOnline/77790)
Former UN envoy Nikolai Mladenov, tasked with Hamas disarmament, asserted in an interview that disarmament will happen. (Source: @amitsegal/63744)
Hamas reaffirmed full commitment to the 15-point roadmap agreed with mediators, contrasting with Netanyahu's outright rejection. (Source: @presstv/202178)

Netanyahu's cabinet reiterated that no pullback will occur until "genuine disarmament" of Hamas, encompassing all weapon categories, and rejected any Palestinian statehood. (Source: @VahidOnline/77790, @presstv/202178)
Iran's six conditions for Strait of Hormuz reopening include demand for end to US attacks on Iranian allies in Lebanon, linking Lebanese front to Gulf waterway leverage. (Source: @VahidOnline/77788)
Iran's conditions also require cessation of US attacks on allies in Iraq and Yemen, broadening the linkage beyond Gaza and Lebanon. (Source: @VahidOnline/77788)

A US official disclosed approximately 8 million barrels of oil per night transit the southern Strait of Hormuz corridor under US military coordination; Washington aims to increase this volume before any agreement. (Source: @kianmeli1/90768, @rodast_omiddana/79032)
An unnamed source claimed the Strait of Hormuz will lose 50-70% of its current energy transit importance within two years as underground pipelines replace maritime routes. (Source: @mamlekate/104107)
Reports attribute a drone downed in southern Iran to Saudi origin, indicating possible Saudi aerial activity near Iranian airspace. (Source: @naya_foriraq/87425)
Houthi forces in Yemen reportedly attacked Mocha port, controlled by UAE-backed forces, continuing Red Sea maritime pressure. (Source: @New_security8200/203250)

sections.threat_assessment: Iran's appointment of Rezaei and its maximalist Strait conditions signal a hardened posture linking Gulf energy security to regional conflicts in Gaza, Lebanon, Yemen, and Iraq. Netanyahu's absolute rejection of the Trump plan and insistence on total Hamas disarmament eliminates near-term diplomatic off-ramps. The US-driven oil flow maintenance through the Strait undercuts Iranian leverage but risks escalation if Iran tests red lines. Unverified drone attacks and Houthi port strikes indicate expanding kinetic activity across maritime domains. The Saudi drone incident suggests growing aerial friction along the Gulf's western littoral.
sections.regional_response: Gulf states monitor the Strait standoff closely; the claim that pipelines will supplant 50-70% of Hormuz transit within two years reflects strategic hedging. Saudi Arabia's alleged drone penetration of southern Iran, if confirmed, marks a shift from proxy to direct aerial confrontation. UAE-backed forces in Yemen absorbing Houthi attacks on Mocha port demonstrate continued Red Sea vulnerability. Oman's mediation channel remains active but subordinate to US-Iran bilateral dynamics. Regional actors are preparing for prolonged confrontation rather than imminent breakthrough.
sections.intelligence_notes: The simultaneous hardening of Iranian and Israeli positions reduces mediation space; Rezaei's SNSC role may accelerate decision-making for coercive maritime actions. The six conditions are likely non-negotiable for Washington, making Strait closure a persistent threat. Oil flow data suggests US naval presence sustains throughput despite Iranian rhetoric. The Saudi drone incident warrants verification; if true, it indicates Saudi willingness to challenge Iranian air defenses. Houthi targeting of Mocha port aligns with pattern of striking UAE-linked infrastructure.
